evidence.text: Reason for referral: Progressive exertional shortness of breath and ankle swelling over two months in a 77-year-old woman with hypertension and known coronary artery disease.

Findings: Sinus rhythm at 62 bpm. Left axis deviation. PR interval 180 ms, QRS 104 ms, QTc 446 ms. Q waves in leads II, III, and aVF.
Impression: Sinus rhythm with left axis deviation and inferior Q waves consistent with prior inferior infarct.

Findings: Normal left ventricular size. Left ventricular ejection fraction estimated at 45%. Hypokinesis of the inferior wall. Mild mitral regurgitation. Normal left atrial size. No pericardial effusion.
Impression: Mildly reduced left ventricular systolic function with inferior wall hypokinesis.

LIPID PANEL
Total Cholesterol: 162 mg/dL
LDL Cholesterol: 84 mg/dL
HDL Cholesterol: 48 mg/dL
Triglycerides: 150 mg/dL

BASIC METABOLIC PANEL
Sodium: 137 mmol/L
Potassium: 4.5 mmol/L
Chloride: 101 mmol/L
CO2: 24 mmol/L
BUN: 22 mg/dL
Creatinine: 1.0 mg/dL
Glucose: 101 mg/dL (H)
Calcium: 9.1 mg/dL

Metoprolol tartrate 25 mg by mouth twice daily
Amlodipine 10 mg by mouth once daily
Atorvastatin 40 mg by mouth once daily
Aspirin 81 mg by mouth once daily
2. Coronary artery disease, stable without angina. Continue metoprolol tartrate 50 mg twice daily and aspirin.

EXAM:
General: comfortable at rest, mildly breathless when walking to the exam room.
Neck: mild jugular venous distension at 45 degrees.
Cardiac exam: regular rhythm, normal S1 and S2, soft systolic murmur at the left sternal border, no gallop.
Lungs: faint bibasilar crackles.
Extremities: 1+ pitting edema of both ankles.
